assertions.name: control_free_state_is_the_induced_product
assertions.source: disjoint character vs LR prediction, sublemma-2-1-deuteron-branching

description: Across the proton|neutron cut H_3 (x) H_3 < H_6 the free state is a product (S=0) and every state has S >= 0, so dS >= 0 is a THEOREM. Measured exactly: the per-block cut entropy is non-negative on all 11 blocks, zero on exactly the two one-dimensional ones, and conjugation invariant. The committed binding_von_neumann_entropy_probe reports dS < 0 for 2 of 3 isotopes, so its quantity -- a Shannon entropy over Wedderburn blocks of the whole algebra, with no bipartition, no partial trace and no reduced density matrix -- is not an entanglement entropy and its 'von Neumann entanglement' label is wrong.

data.cut: H_3 (x) H_3 < H_6 (proton strands | neutron strands)

caveats: Scope (a). Establishes that dS >= 0 is forced across any bipartition, hence that the committed probe's quantity is not an entanglement entropy -- it is a Shannon entropy over Wedderburn blocks of the whole algebra. That probe's arithmetic is not disputed and is not re-run; only its LABEL is refuted, and I relayed that label without checking it.

NOT claimed: that E_0 * S_cut is the binding energy, or that this cut entropy appears in any binding formula. The value AME would require lies inside the measured range [0, 1.4708], and that is a GENERICITY observation rather than evidence -- a weighting over eleven blocks spanning that interval can be made to hit almost anything in it. No weighting is chosen and no binding contribution is computed.

Entanglement cost is NOT excluded as an ingredient. The earlier probe refutes one prescription; this one refutes that prescription's label. Neither bears on whether a correctly-defined cut entropy plays a role.
